subject: Failover consistency & regional erase behavior — DR/backups Qs
messages:
From: Samantha Lewis <samantha@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: infra@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-20T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Question: how deletes propagate during failover / regional lockdown?

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our SOC/DR questionnaire and have a couple of fairly specific follow-ups from security on backup retention and deletion propagation. Two practical scenarios they want clarified: 

1) If ACME triggers a data deletion request (customer-initiated erase) and then there is an unplanned failover from us-west to us-east, what guarantees do you have that the deletion will not reappear from an older snapshot/replica?

2) If a region is placed into an operational lockdown for a legal hold or investigation (no writes allowed), how do backups taken during that period behave with respect to later retention sweeps? Can we get an explicit window for when a deleted object becomes irrecoverable (for legal timeline purposes)?

We included a preliminary manifest of the buckets/ids below in case that helps. Could you confirm the risk profile and any mitigation controls we can list in the questionnaire?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lewis
Senior Cloud Security, ACME Corp

Attachments: acme-backup-manifest.csv
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha@acme.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: how deletes propagate during failover / regional lockdown?

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear scenarios and the manifest. I pulled together a short answer and attached our DR playbook excerpt that covers the deterministic behavior. High level:

- Deletion model: we enforce a three-layer deletion flow: API delete -> metadata tombstone + retention marker -> asynchronous retention sweep that removes content blobs and snapshot references. The tombstone is written to the control plane and replicated synchronously to all regions before we acknowledge the delete to the customer.

- Failover behavior: because the tombstone and retention marker are control-plane replicated synchronously (with leader-quorum write), any subsequent failover that mounts a snapshot will check the tombstones at mount time; snapshots that reference deleted objects are rewritten on mount to prune the deleted entries. That means an acknowledged delete should not re-materialize after a region failover.

- Lockdown/legal-hold scenario: when a region is marked as locked for investigation, we stop automated retention sweeps for that region and flag snapshots as "investigation hold". Those snapshots are excluded from expiration until the hold is lifted by the customer/legal owner. We can provide an audit entry for the hold start/end times.

- Irrecoverability window: practical irrecoverability occurs after the retention sweep completes and the tombstone TTL expires in auxiliary replication caches. For our standard configuration (7-day tombstone TTL + async sweep every 24 hours) the expected irrecoverability window is 8 days from the acknowledged delete. If you require a shorter or contractually guaranteed window we can map to a dedicated retention profile (e.g., 48-hour tombstone TTL + manual sweep) under a Dedicated/Private plan.

I'll attach the redwood-dr-playbook.pdf excerpt that shows the exact sequence diagrams and the relevant config knobs. Also looping in Markus and Lauren for confirmation on contract-level guarantees and audit exports.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dr-playbook.pdf

On a related note: can you confirm whether ACME's legal hold will be region-scoped or account-scoped? That changes how we model snapshot immutability in cross-region replication.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lewis <samantha@acme.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-24T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: how deletes propagate during failover / regional lockdown?

Samantha — quick add from a contractual/controls perspective:

- We can commit to the synchronous tombstone replication behavior in a SOC2/Enterprise addendum. That gives you an auditable event that a delete was acknowledged and replicated.
- For account-scoped legal holds we recommend a multi-region hold policy: we freeze retention sweeps globally for the account and surface a single audit timeline. Region-scoped holds are supported but require per-region hold lift confirmations (we'll record them).
- If ACME requires a cryptographic proof-of-erasure (hash-based evidence of blob deletion), we have an optional erasure log export we can enable for Dedicated/Private customers; it's not enabled by default for Hosted customers for performance reasons.

Olga/Connor — can operations run a short simulation for ACME that demonstrates a delete + failover (us-west -> us-east) and produce the audit trail? Samantha — we'll ship the results and a short narrated recording.

-Markus
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lewis <samantha@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: infra@acme.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-01T14:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Question: how deletes propagate during failover / regional lockdown?

Thanks — that addresses our main concerns and the playbook excerpt is helpful. ACME will review the 8-day default window with legal; we may request a tighter SLA for a subset of customers.

Region scope: we'll plan for an account-wide hold initially, so your multi-region guidance fits our needs. Please proceed with the simulation you proposed and share the recording + audit export (HUBSPOT-ACME-8921). If you can include the manifest lines I sent in the simulation, that would be ideal.

I'll open a follow-up if we formalize an SLA change. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Samantha
